recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed unless the work group makes a new decision to restore a maintained EPUB/FHIR Book artifact with a conformant generation process.
issue_request: FHIR-7779 was a Published FHIR-core issue with Persuasive with Modification resolution. It reported that fhir-v0.5.0.epub opened to the cover in iBooks on Mac OS X Yosemite but then failed as corrupt, with the accepted resolution to remove the EPUB if it could not be fixed and a later Jira comment saying it was fixed.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-7779, #7779, or ballot comment #1100 was found. The issue appears to have concerned a generated DSTU1 publication artifact rather than a maintained current source file. The only current git-tracked EPUB-related files are old tools/epub packaging templates, and the current source tree has no fhir-v0.5.0.epub artifact or link.
additional_context: The later Published EPUB issue FHIR-8613 records the broader resolution that the FHIR Book EPUB was withdrawn because epubcheck conformance was not practical with the HTML5-based specification. That withdrawal was applied in Subversion revision 6712, imported as git commit ac5f9b4d98e50aa779bfc1454fdb8cdd0db0bf91, by commenting out the downloads-page FHIR Book row. A separate AutoFHIR audit commit for FHIR-8613 already exists on the combined branch and confirms the active downloads page remains EPUB-free.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build source does not publish or advertise the obsolete DSTU1 EPUB, so there is no remaining current-spec correction for FHIR-7779.

related_jiras.note: Later Published issue withdrew the FHIR Book EPUB after determining conformance was impractical; it is already represented on the combined branch by commit 4671abacb8da1bbe8e477a2eefc842258515a53d.
